instruction: Search Google Scholar for AI researcher Fei-Fei Li and add one entry with her information to the researchers.xlsx file on Desktop as a new row (row 6). Include her name, all citations, h-index, i10-index, top cited work title, and PDF link of the top cited work.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1)

required_fields.field: PDF Link of Top Cited Work

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching Google Scholar for Fei-Fei Li and adding her information to row 6 of the Excel file, similar to the original task pattern (Yann LeCun). The evaluator checks that row 6 contains: (1) Name field contains 'Fei-Fei Li' (partial credit 1/6), (2-6) All other required fields exist and are non-null (partial credit for each field). Total score is sum of matches / 6. This maintains similar complexity to original task. Custom getter reads row 6 data, metric checks field presence with partial scoring. Includes postconfig to save file.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Partial credit: 1/6 for name containing 'Fei-Fei Li', 1/6 each for the 5 other fields being non-null (citations, h-index, i10-index, top work, PDF link)

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is semantically correct and can verify all 6 instruction requirements
Getter correctly extracts row 6 data from Excel file with proper column header mapping
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' (receives rules dict directly, not nested structure)
Partial credit scoring logic is sound: 1/6 for name contains check, 1/6 for each of 5 existence checks
Postconfig appropriately saves file with Ctrl+S before verification
Name field uses 'contains' check which is flexible for variations (e.g., 'Dr. Fei-Fei Li')
Other fields only check existence (non-null), which is appropriate since citation metrics vary over time
Static warning about dict vs Dict type compatibility is a false positive (both are valid type hints)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor risk: Evaluator assumes specific column headers ('Name', 'All citations', 'h-index', etc.) exist in researchers.xlsx. If actual headers differ slightly (e.g., 'Researcher Name' vs 'Name'), field matching will fail. This is reasonable given task context but worth noting.
Consider adding fallback logic or case-insensitive header matching if header name variations are expected
